title: Extraction with log n plus constant seed length
formal:
Is there an explicit family of ordinary seeded extractors with error at most \(1/100\), a rational constant \(\gamma\in(0,1]\) and an integer constant \(C\ge0\) such that, for all integers \(n\ge2\) and \(0\le k\le n\),
\[\operatorname{Ext}_{n,k}:\{0,1\}^{n}\times\{0,1\}^{d(n,k)}\to\{0,1\}^{m(n,k)},\qquad d(n,k)\le\lceil\log_2 n\rceil+C,\qquad m(n,k)\ge\lfloor\gamma k\rfloor?\]
For every distribution \(X\) on \(n\)-bit strings satisfying \(H_{\infty}(X)\ge k\), and a uniform seed independent of \(X\), the required guarantee is
\[\operatorname{TV}\bigl(\operatorname{Ext}_{n,k}(X,U_{d(n,k)}),U_{m(n,k)}\bigr)\le1/100.\]
The family, \(C\), \(\gamma\) and its polynomial evaluation bound must be uniform across \(n,k\). This selects the main \(m=\Omega(k)\) target in Vadhan's Open Problem 6.42, retaining its weaker polynomial-output alternative as context.
why: A logarithmic seed is often enumerated over all possibilities. Fixing its leading coefficient at one makes that enumeration linear in the source length up to a constant factor, instead of an unspecified polynomial. Achieving substantial output at that seed length for arbitrary min-entropy would sharpen a central resource bound in explicit randomness extraction.
status_note: Open Problem 6.42 was read directly on 2026-09-14. A bounded later-work search and inspection of the 2022 short-seed theorem and February 2026 Doron–Ribeiro revision found no matching construction or refutation for coefficient-one seed length and constant-fraction output across every entropy threshold. Current openness is source-based, not an exhaustive literature certification.

progress.text: Open Problem 6.42 asks for seed length log n plus an additive constant at error 0.01, with a constant fraction of k output bits as the main target.

The JACM paper Nearly Optimal Pseudorandomness from Hardness includes a finer short-seed extractor in a restricted entropy regime, with a coefficient above one and the output tradeoff stated in Theorem 1.7.
The Doron–Ribeiro revision gives faster evaluation with an order-optimal logarithmic seed, rather than the additive-optimal seed bound required here.

sentences: This question asks how close an efficiently computable extractor can get to the minimum useful seed length.
It requires at most the base-two logarithm of the source length plus a constant number of seed bits.
The output must contain a fixed positive fraction of the source entropy and have statistical error at most one hundredth.
One deterministic polynomial-time family must meet these guarantees for every source length and entropy threshold.
Known constructions in the checked sources optimize related parameters but do not supply this full combination.

definitions:
The parameters \(n,k,d,m\) are nonnegative integer bit lengths, with the domain restrictions in the statement and \(m\le n+d\). The latter is a harmless output-length normalization. All logarithms have base two. Min-entropy is \(H_{\infty}(X)=-\log_2\max_x\Pr[X=x]\), so the source promise bounds every point mass by \(2^{-k}\). No efficient sampling assumption, independence between source coordinates or extra side-information promise is imposed. The extractor gets \(x,y\), not a source distribution or its support. The seed distribution \(U_d\) assigns equal probability to each \(d\)-bit string and is independent of the source. \(U_0\) is the point mass at the empty string. Statistical distance is \(\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)=\frac12\sum_z|P(z)-Q(z)|\).

Explicitness means that two fixed deterministic multitape Turing machines, using no advice or oracle, compute the parameters on \((1^n,k)\) and the full output on \((1^n,k,x,y)\), respectively. Here \(k\) is binary, \(|x|=n\), and \(|y|=d(n,k)\). There are fixed integers \(K,q\ge1\) such that each computation, including preprocessing and writing its output, halts within \(K(n+1)^q\) steps for every valid input. The parameters must be computed by the family; they cannot depend on the unknown source. Correctness is statistical for every promised distribution, even one with no efficient sampler.

The extractor is ordinary: the output alone must be close to uniform. Uniformity conditional on a separately disclosed seed is not an additional requirement. The seed may contribute bits to the ordinary output, which is why a nontrivial source-output condition is expressed uniformly over all \(k\). The fixed coefficient one in \(\lceil\log_2 n\rceil+C\) is essential: a bound \(A\log n\) with unspecified \(A>1\) need not qualify. Rounding changes the seed length and minimum output by at most one bit and does not alter the additive-constant and constant-fraction target.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of existence or nonexistence of the specified uniform family. Existence requires algorithms and universal constants proving the seed bound with logarithmic coefficient one, output at least \(\lfloor\gamma k\rfloor\), statistical error at most \(1/100\) for every promised source, and polynomial evaluation time for all \(n,k\). A refutation must rule out every such choice. A construction for a restricted entropy range, a seed bound \((1+\delta)\log_2 n+O(1)\) with fixed \(\delta>0\), or merely \(k^{\beta}\) output for fixed \(\beta<1\), is insufficient for this selected main target.

context_blocks.text: The source explicitly separates two improvements over constant-factor-optimal extraction: constant total entropy loss, and a seed of \(\log_2 n+O(1)\) bits. This card concerns the latter and does not require constant loss.

Open Problem 6.42 presents \(\Omega(k)\) output as its main target and also asks about the weaker possibility of \(k^{\Omega(1)}\) output. The card makes the constant-fraction target precise; it does not treat the two as equivalent.

Doron, Moshkovitz, Oh and Zuckerman obtain short seeds in a substantial entropy regime. Their Theorem 1.7 gives seed length \((1+c\alpha)\log n+c\log(1/\varepsilon)\) and output of order \(n^{1-2\alpha}\) for entropy at least \(n^{1-\alpha}\), under the stated parameter conditions. This is a finer seed bound than unspecified \(O(\log n)\), but for fixed positive \(\alpha\) it does not meet coefficient one or constant-fraction output throughout the card’s domain.

The 2026 revised Doron–Ribeiro theorem improves the running time of constructions with \(O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\) seed length and a constant fraction of the entropy as output, with entropy and preprocessing qualifications. Its asymptotic seed bound leaves the leading constant unspecified.
